pins.definition: A piece of special glass in which you can see your reflection.
A piece of glass with a shiny backing that reflects images.
A smooth glass surface that reflects images.

situation: A young woman in a dimly lit hallway leans in close to check her hair before leaving the house.
subject: the reflection
brief: A young woman stands before an ornate, oval wall glass framed in carved, flowing wooden vines, and her own face stares back at her with perfect clarity from the gleaming surface. The frame is the brightest and most detailed object in the dim hallway, catching the warm evening light.
prompt: A young woman stands before an ornate, oval wall glass framed in carved, flowing wooden vines, and her own face stares back at her with perfect clarity from the gleaming surface. The frame is the brightest and most detailed object in the dim hallway, catching the warm evening light. art nouveau in the manner of Mucha, sinuous ornamental linework and flowing organic curves, muted jewel tones with gold leaf, a decorative arch or halo of pattern behind the figure. The ornament stays behind and around the subject and never competes with it: the pattern frames what matters rather than filling the frame. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
